item.text: I’ll inspect the service documentation first, then build a temporary read-only reconciliation script that handles pagination, token refreshes, rate limits, deduplication, UTC filtering, and per-order half-up rounding. I’ll leave only the required `result.json` in `/workspace`.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The docs confirm 50-item pagination and bearer-token authentication. I’m now querying every page and caching customer records; the temporary collector will retry authentication and rate-limit responses rather than treating either as an endpoint failure.

The full traversal completed successfully: 407 distinct qualifying shipped orders were found, with 20 duplicate listings discarded. I’m doing the final file/schema and arithmetic checks now, including verifying the regional sum equals the total.
